verdictText: **APPROVE-WITH-NOTES.** No blockers, no majors. The three product leaves implement the registered behaviour; the red-first proof is genuine; the census fits (10 of 15 files, 336 of 500 counted lines, re-derived); the seven restriction leaves (two of them unchanged) and the unit's own lifecycle fields are the only changes; the route still reaches only the old create; the new public codes carry no private state; 5 of 7 of my behaviour mutants are caught by the registered suites and the 2 survivors are coverage gaps, not defects. Decision point 1 (the post-red stabilisation of the cross-process case) is ruled a disclosed, assertion-monotone harness change that does not weaken what the case proves; the RED-byte test file passes 3/3 against the head product in the registered run mode, so the product is proven against the red bytes as well. Minors M1-M5 and notes N1-N6 require no change to this head. Carry-forwards for P2CG1D are in section 7.

reviewClassEvidence.note: The unit's five sensitive review classes, each with the reviewer's section 5 finding verbatim. The reviewer records no finding in any class; concurrency carries two design hazards for successors (N2, N3) as carry-forwards CF-D5 and CF-D7. Each verdict field is the closure's reading of the finding, not reviewer text.

authority.finding: **Authority.** No new trust surface. `actorId` comes from the route's authenticated player; `createPreparedCoopMissionMatch` is a server module export with no route, socket or client reach (section 6 item 4). Membership is re-checked at the same three points as the baseline; admission, roster and fingerprint identity rules are shared with the route path through one body rather than copied. The P2CB preparation is opaque (a `WeakMap` capture inside `campaignPublicAppliedView.ts`), is revalidated only by the view that created it, and only on that graph's own handle inside an open transaction; a second module graph's view on the same file is refused `context-mismatch` -> `COOP_MISSION_LAUNCH_REFUSED` with both files unwritten (tested, including a cold reopen). The old route-reached create needs no readiness and still answers 201 (positive control in the first case). No finding.

privacy.finding: **Privacy.** The three new public codes `COOP_MISSION_LAUNCH_UNSUPPORTED`, `COOP_MISSION_NOT_CONVERGED` and `COOP_MISSION_LAUNCH_REFUSED` are `CoopMissionRefusal(409, code)` instances whose only own properties are `status`, `code`, `name` and `message === code`; the verdict's `reason`, `participantIds`, cuts, digests and hydration are dropped at `launchRefusal` (`expectPublicOnly` pins the serialised shape; my RM4 shows the pin discriminates). The route maps `CoopMissionRefusal` to `{error: code, code}` and everything else, including `CoopMissionCommitError` (whose `errors` can carry SQLite messages), to a fixed `500 COOP_MISSION_STORE_FAILURE` after server-side logging. `ICampaignLaunchPreparation` carries no journal position, digest or row fingerprint (its own doc comment and the capture design). No finding.

replay.finding: **Replay.** Match id, request fingerprint, owner map, side assignments and the opening events are derived by the same code as the route path; the lock-order case proves one deterministic match and opening log through a cold reopen (`GameCreated`, `GameStarted` prefix equal across the owning store and an independent handle). The seed after release is the baseline `seedJournalFromInitialEvents` (idempotent on its receipt). The route then reaches the same stored identity through the old door without a second match or a second launch event. No finding.

idempotency.finding: **Idempotency.** Exact retry after a precommit failure creates once; after a known M commit with a failed C release, the retry settles from the stored row (`prepare` not called: no new readiness granted), announces once and appends one launch; after an uncertain outcome the retry's readback finds no row and creates once; after campaign advancement the stored identity is returned with no append and identity/membership still apply (divergent config -> `COOP_MISSION_IDENTITY_CONFLICT`; revoked seat -> 403). `holdMatchConnection.release` and the reservation's `release` are idempotent and inert after the microtask. No finding.

concurrency.verdict: PASS (no finding on this head; carry-forwards CF-D5 and CF-D7)
concurrency.finding: **Concurrency.** Lock order is C IMMEDIATE then M IMMEDIATE, pinned by the exec trail `C:BEGIN IMMEDIATE, M:BEGIN IMMEDIATE, M:COMMIT, C:ROLLBACK` and by the observation that during the guard both handles are in a transaction and a separate connection cannot take either file's write lock; at M COMMIT the row is visible on the owning connection and not yet on a read-only one, and C is still held. A real second process sees BUSY on both files during the hold and acquires each lock only after the corresponding release (match after M COMMIT, campaign after C ROLLBACK). A competing process that commits first makes the IMMEDIATE acquisition wait and the revalidation refuse `COOP_MISSION_NOT_CONVERGED` with an unchanged census, while a deferred reader on the same file keeps its stale snapshot and cannot upgrade (`SQLITE_BUSY*`). There is no `await` between `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` on C and `ROLLBACK` on C (the write callback is synchronous; `create` is the synchronous store method; `revalidate` is synchronous and thenables are rejected). Nothing holds M across an `await` either: the store's microtask release is proven by the forgotten-hold case (a write made inside a forgotten reservation is rolled back by the next microtask and a stale release is inert). Finding: none on this head; two design hazards for successors are recorded as N2 (stuck transaction after a throwing ROLLBACK) and N3 (deferred read-then-write on M under external writers), with carry-forwards CF-D5 and CF-D7.

decisionPoint1: **Decision point 1: the test changed after the RED commit.** The diff between 8f0955f8 and ed7fb95b in `coopMissionCreate.test.ts` is +23/-2, all inside the `blocked` branch of the spawned child script and the `blocks writers in other processes ...` case. Red version: after observing BUSY, the child immediately did `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` (busy_timeout 15 s), wrote a probe row and committed, so the saga writer's commit could land on matches.db while the parent's post-release `seedJournalFromInitialEvents` had a DEFERRED read transaction open. Head version: the child proves the lock is free with `BEGIN IMMEDIATE`/`ROLLBACK` (recording `acquiredAt`), waits for a `.done` marker the parent writes after `create()` resolves, then commits its probe; one assertion is added (`committedAt >= acquiredAt`), none removed or loosened. The kept flake log (`green-related-run1-flake.json`, sha256 verified) shows exactly one failure in 1490 tests: `SqliteError: database is locked` thrown at `DurableMatchStore.ts:1260` inside `seedJournalFromInitialEvents`'s `db.transaction` (the INSERT after the receipt SELECT), i.e. `SQLITE_BUSY_SNAPSHOT` on a deferred write upgrade, which `busy_timeout` does not retry. Ruling: (a) this is not a violation of the red/green discipline's purpose. The discipline exists so that the product is proven against tests the author did not tune after seeing it fail; here the product never failed the case in the registered run mode (my 3/3 runs of the RED-byte file against the head product, and the author's two-suite green), the only failure was a timing race between two OS processes in a parallel selection the discipline does not register, the change is to the child harness's scheduling and is assertion-monotone, and it was disclosed with the raw evidence. It is a recorded deviation from byte-identity, not a hidden one, and the author's mutation probes ran against the red bytes. (b) The case still proves what its title says: `busyAt <= guardAt` (both writers were refused during the hold), `saga.acquiredAt >= matchCommit` and `campaign.acquiredAt >= campaignRelease` (each lock became takeable only after the matching release) are unchanged, and the commit now lands after the parent's post-release work rather than concurrently with it. What moved is only that "then lets them commit" is no longer demonstrated to be concurrent with the parent's seed, which was never the claim. (c) The underlying behaviour the flake exposed is real but baseline: every `this.db.transaction(fn)()` on DurableMatchStore is BEGIN DEFERRED and reads before it writes, so under any concurrent writer in another process on matches.db a write upgrade can fail with `SQLITE_BUSY_SNAPSHOT` instead of waiting. Production runs one server process on matches.db and the route path has the same exposure, so this is not C's defect and not in C's leaves to fix; it is recorded as N3 and carried to D as CF-D5 (D must not add a deferred read-then-write on M, and E's route switch must keep seed/recovery/announce after both releases). I would have preferred the stabilisation to be committed as a separate, visibly labelled fourth commit rather than folded into the implementation commit; that is M1, a docs/ledger minor.

**C-OPEN-1 / CF-C1 non-applicability.** Confirmed by the code and by the trail: the only SQL C issues on the campaign handle is `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` and `ROLLBACK` (the `traceExec` spy records every `exec`, and `holdCampaign`'s write callback cannot reach `appendInBorrowedTransaction` or any journal writer: the create module imports no campaign sync or journal module, only the type-only `campaignPublicAppliedView`). `revalidate` reads the branch store, effective head, roster and applied-view rows and writes nothing (the only INSERT/UPDATE in `campaignPublicAppliedView.ts` is in `accept`, not on this path). CF-C1 therefore does not arise; no leaf outside the seven is implied.

**Refusal precedence and ordering.** Not ready at `prepare` (fresh-request, participants-behind, saga/precedence refusal, context-mismatch, integrity) refuses before any SQL; `readmit()` (STALE_HEAD) runs after the preparation and before the C hold, outside SQL; inside the hold the guard's order is context -> precedence (saga/branch/manifest, `unavailable` distinct from known absence: the unreadable-saga case) -> input drift (`not-converged fresh-request`), and the five drift cases pin the public code for each. STALE_HEAD before the hold is the right place (the re-admission reads in-memory host state, not SQL), but it is not covered on the prepared path (RM2); see M4.

**Dormancy (CF-C8, re-run at the head).** `git grep` over `src` and `server.js` excluding `__tests__` and B's six leaves for `applyHostIntentWithControls|appendControlledCommandBatch|appendInBorrowedTransaction|afterRelease|CAMPAIGN_APPEND_CONTROLS_UNSUPPORTED` finds only declarations (`ICampaignEventStore.ts:137/236`, `campaignHostBatchCommit.ts:91`), no caller. `createPreparedCoopMissionMatch`, `createMatchPrepared`, `reserveMatchProgression` and `CoopMissionCommitError` have no production caller; the only production use of the create module is `src/pages/api/multiplayer/matches/index.ts:315 -> createCoopMissionMatch`. `bindCampaignSyncConnection.ts:910` and `CampaignGmArbiter.ts:453` still call the uncontrolled `applyHostIntent`; `server.js`, the registry, binder, arbiter, Protocol and receipt port are unchanged. The first case also proves the route still reaches the old create at runtime (201 with `createMatchPrepared` never called).

**Guidance for P2CG1D ("`reserveMatchProgression` inside B's guard, release in `onCommitted`") is sound, with three conditions.** (i) It is synchronous end to end: B's `guard(db)` runs inside `appendWithExtension`'s `.immediate()` transaction (writer lines 74-82) and the writer calls `onCommitted` synchronously after COMMIT before the promise settles, so a reservation taken in the guard is still held at `onCommitted`; the store's microtask release fires only after that whole span. (ii) The adapter calls D's `onCommitted` only when a batch was actually recorded (`committed !== null`, `JournalCampaignEventStore.ts:393-401`): on a refused guard or a duplicate the explicit release never runs and the microtask releases M. That is safe but D should release explicitly on its refusal return too and treat the microtask as the net. (iii) `reserveMatchProgression()` throws when M is already in a transaction, and a throw inside B's guard is `commit-uncertain` (CF-C2), so D's guard must catch and return a typed refusal. Lock order is the same C-then-M in both units, so the two paths cannot deadlock across processes, and within a process neither spans an await. CF-D1..CF-D4 carry the exact wording.

**Carry-forward compliance.** CF-C1 N/A (item 2). CF-C2 honoured in spirit at the match owner: `refused` is the only nothing-written arm, a guard throw is a precommit throw (nothing written, original error kept), a failed COMMIT is resolved by owner readback, `uncertain` only when the readback itself fails, and the create-level `CoopMissionCommitError('uncertain')` is settled on retry by `readMission` readback, never by compensation. CF-C3 honoured: the optional method is the capability, no boolean, memory store refused before effects. CF-C4 N/A (no controlled door is called); the outcome arms added here are the match-side analogue and `settlePreparedCreate` switches them exhaustively (`result.kind` narrowing plus `HeldCreate`). CF-C5 N/A (no `afterRelease`); the reservation release is idempotent and readback-observable as CF-C5 will require. CF-C6 N/A (no writer `onCommitted` caller). CF-C7 honoured: no Protocol/wire/identity change; the B identity-equality fixture passes unchanged (45/45). CF-C8 honoured (item 4). CF-C9 honoured and recorded in the admission and local receipts; my figures agree (section 3). CF-C10 honoured: 32 names verified on the exact head. C-OPEN-2 honoured (M4 not absorbed; `JournalCampaignEventStore.test.ts` untouched). C-OPEN-3 honoured (B main-verified in the baseline ledger; grep and lint/madge re-measured at 8fde3b97). B's M1-M4 and N1-N5 were informational for C except M4 (not absorbed, correctly) and N1 (see N2 below, which gives N1 a new way to arise).

carryForwards.wording: **CF-D1 (reservation is write-free and synchronous).** `reserveMatchProgression()` is `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` on DurableMatchStore's own M connection with only `release()` (ROLLBACK, idempotent) and no commit; a queued microtask rolls back whatever its synchronous span left open. Any M write made while the reservation is held (including store methods such as `appendEvents`/`appendCommandBatch`, which nest as SAVEPOINTs via `db.transaction`) is discarded by the release while the method reports success. D must make no M write inside the reservation, and the span from `reserveMatchProgression()` to `release()` must contain no `await`.

**CF-D2 (placement inside B's guard).** B's `guard(db)` runs synchronously inside `appendWithExtension`'s `.immediate()` transaction on C and the writer calls `onCommitted` synchronously after COMMIT in the same span (`SQLiteEventJournalWriter.ts:74-82`), so a reservation taken in the guard is still held at `onCommitted`. The adapter invokes D's `onCommitted` only when a batch was actually recorded (`committed !== null`); on a refused guard or a duplicate the explicit release never runs and the microtask releases M. Release explicitly on both the guard's refusal return and `onCommitted`; treat the microtask only as the safety net.

carryForwards.concern: M-busy must be a refusal, not an uncertain commit
carryForwards.wording: **CF-D3 (M-busy must be a refusal, not an uncertain commit).** `reserveMatchProgression()` throws `Match reservation needs an idle match connection` when M is already in a transaction. A throw from inside B's guard is classified `commit-uncertain` (CF-C2) and demands a receipt readback. D's guard must catch that throw and return a typed `{kind:'refused', reason}` arm.

**CF-D4 (lock order).** C's prepared create takes C IMMEDIATE then M IMMEDIATE; D's door takes C IMMEDIATE (the writer's `.immediate()`) then M (the reservation inside the guard). Keep C-then-M in every new door; never take M before C on a path that can later touch C; never hold either across an await.

**CF-D5 (deferred reads on M).** Every existing `this.db.transaction(fn)()` on DurableMatchStore is BEGIN DEFERRED and reads before it writes; under a concurrent writer in another process the write upgrade fails with `SQLITE_BUSY_SNAPSHOT` (message `database is locked`), which `busy_timeout` does not retry. This is baseline exposure (the kept flake `green-related-run1-flake.json`: `seedJournalFromInitialEvents` at `DurableMatchStore.ts:1260`), not a C defect. D must not add a deferred read-then-write on M on any reservation path, and E's route switch must keep seed, recovery and announcement after both releases exactly as C does.

**CF-D6 (readback and identity).** `createMatchPrepared` classifies a failed COMMIT by `getMatchRow(meta.matchId).meta_json === JSON.stringify(meta)` (exact identity, not row presence) and answers `uncertain` only when the release or the readback itself threw. D's analogue on C is B's `getCommandReceipt`; do not add a presence-only check anywhere on either side.

**CF-D7 (stuck-transaction hazard).** `holdMatchConnection.release` and `holdCampaign` mark the hold released before ROLLBACK; a throwing ROLLBACK leaves that connection in a transaction nothing retries. The next prepared hold on it refuses (`needs an idle ... connection`), which is fail-closed, but ordinary `db.transaction()` callers on the same connection would then nest as SAVEPOINTs without durability (B's N1). D's door must keep B's `onCommitted` request (which forces the writer's in-transaction refusal) and must treat `db.inTransaction === true` before its BEGIN as a refusal, never as a nested transaction.

notes.wording: **N1:** the duplicate pre-check in `writeMatchRows` runs inside the IMMEDIATE hold on the prepared path and outside any transaction on the async path (baseline behaviour, where the UNIQUE constraint remains the backstop); this is why `refuses a borrowed transaction and a duplicate id without writing` can assert `already exists` with nothing written.

**N2:** both `holdMatchConnection.release` and `holdCampaign` set `held=false` (or return) before ROLLBACK runs; if ROLLBACK itself threw, the connection would remain in a transaction with no retry, and only the next prepared hold would notice (fail-closed). ROLLBACK failing in better-sqlite3 requires an I/O error or an open statement iterator, neither of which this code can produce; this is a design note for CF-D7, not a finding.

**N3:** the flake's root cause is the DEFERRED `db.transaction` in `seedJournalFromInitialEvents` (and every other `db.transaction` on M) under a concurrent external writer; see section 6 item 1(c) and CF-D5. In the single-process deployment there is no external writer on matches.db; operational scripts opened against a live file would be the only way to reach it today.

**N4:** `CoopMissionCommitError` extends `AggregateError` with `errors` in the order [uncertain error, ...release errors] for `uncertain` and [...release errors] for `committed`; the route would log it and answer the fixed 500 code, so the SQLite text never reaches a client even if E later routes the prepared path.

**N5:** the child process in the cross-process cases is an inline `node -e` script using the installed `better-sqlite3`; no new worker fixture file, so the harness/fixture leaves stayed unchanged as the admission planned. The 15 s child deadlines mean a parent failure before `.done` degrades to a slow test failure, not a hang.
**N6:** `validate-roadmap --next` was not consulted; the plain and `--git` validators pass at the head.
